images.title: A room plan with the girl at the centre
images.purpose: Show that the direction of a thing is said from where a person stands: from the girl at the centre the table is north, the bed is east, the door is south and the cupboard is west.
images.composition: A square room plan from above with a girl at the centre, a table above her, a bed to the right of her, a cupboard to the left of her and a door in the wall below her; four grey arrows run from her with a direction word each; a compass card is at the top right.

In all: 1 room, 4 things (table, cupboard, bed, girl), 1 door, 4 arrows with 4 words, 1 compass card. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: From the girl at the centre, the table is north, the bed is east, the door is south and the cupboard is west.
images.description: A square room plan from above with a girl at the centre, a table above her, a bed on the right, a cupboard on the left and a door below, with four direction arrows and a compass card.
images.context: Concept image for Directions from Where You Stand. It follows the idea of the room picture in your maths book (a girl in a room with a compass beside) and uses this concept's own room plan seen from above, so that above is north.
images.teaching_notes: Stand at the dot with the girl and look up, right, down and left, naming what you find. Then ask: from the bed, where is the girl? The slip to watch: saying the girl is east of the bed, as if the direction stayed the same from both places.

image_decisions.why: The room plan from above with the girl at the centre makes the direction of each thing from her countable and lets the student turn the question round from the bed.
